text:
nina: FYI a partner hit a case where their webhook connector (stripe-invoice-create) returned a model output that passed model-level checks but failed our structured-output gate. Router routed to degen and the customer was billed. Example (redacted): `{"command":"create_invoice","payload":["acct-901", [{"sku":"X","qty":2}]]}` — note `payload` is an array, our schema expects an object `{account_id, line_items}`.

marc: Which cluster and model? Any logs/trace ids?

nina: prod-cc-west, model=open-fin-1. We have trace id `t-1795558888-zz` in observability.

pavel: Router enforces schema gate pre-routing and treats mismatches as hard rejects -> fallback to degen. That's why they saw the degen path.

support-bot: :warning: Alert: schema_rejects rate = 6/min on prod-cc-west (5m)

jen: UX problem: Console surfaces cost and tokens but not the reject reason or whether a coercion could have fixed it. Customers open support tickets asking why they were charged when the model output "looked fine" to them.

marc: Implementation idea: enrich trace/span with `validator.reason`, `validator.hint`, and `validator.coercion_candidate` (a short, redacted diff string). Emit metrics `validation.reject_total{route,model,env}` and `validation.coercion_candidate_total{route,model}`.

pavel: Engineering caution: any coercion must be conservative and reversible. Propose an adapter hook `try_coerce(payload, schema)` that only applies positional->named mapping when mapping rules are explicit (e.g., connector schema declares positional mapping). If applied, produce a reversible diff so we can audit.

jen: Console changes: show a short human-friendly reason ("schema mismatch: payload expected object, got array") in Request Details behind an org-level toggle default OFF. Never reveal raw payload unless org opts in to share validation details.

marc: Rollout modes suggestion: header `x-validate-mode` with values: `observe` (record only), `suggest` (attach suggested coercion to trace but keep original routing), `enforce` (apply coercion/validation and route accordingly). Example config snippet:```validation:
  mode: suggest
  sample_rate: 0.01
  coercions_allowed: [positional_array_to_object]
```

support-bot: :rotating_light: If the spike continues for >10m create `#inc-schema-rejects-prod-cc-west`.

finance-sam: Billing note: we bill for the model attempts that execute. If we later determine a validation misclassification caused an unnecessary fallback, support can issue credits but we need a clear playbook. I'll coordinate with Support to define thresholds for automatic credits.

pavel: Action items: I'll prototype `try_coerce` adapter with reversible diff output and unit tests demonstrating safety rules.

marc: I'll add span enrichment and the two metrics, plus a low-sample observe rollout (1%) to gather baseline.

jen: I'll mock the Console UI with redacted validation hints and a toggle, and draft privacy/consent copy for org settings.

nina: I'll coordinate with finance-sam on billing playbook and support KB.

marc: Quick question: do we want coercion enabled by default for first-party connectors? That feels risky. Recommend opt-in per-org and opt-out by enterprise customers.

pavel: Agreed - default OFF. If we find >95% coercion_success in observe mode then consider a targeted opt-in.

nina: Sync tomorrow 10am to review prototypes. Thanks everyone.
